title: Coupled Penrose vanishing on the round four-sphere

items.title: Positive incidence geometry for the coupled Penrose transform
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Let $S^4={Xin\mathbb R^5:|X|=1}$ have its unit round metric and the orientation which, on the stereographic chart $S^4\setminus\{\infty\}\cong\mathbb R^4$, is $dx_0\wedge dx_1\wedge dx_2\wedge dx_3$. Put $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$, and $r^2=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2$; in these coordinates the metric is $g=4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=0}^3dx_\mu^2$. Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$, put $Z=\mathbb CP^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, and define $\pi:Z\to\mathbb HP^1=S^4$ by $\pi(\ell)=\ell+j\ell$ for a complex line $\ell\subset\mathbb H^2$. Its fibres are projective lines $L_x\cong\mathbb CP^1$. In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$, the fibre over finite $z=(z_1,z_2)$ is the line

$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$

and the fibre over infinity is $L_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Give $Z$ the Fubini–Study metric induced by the standard Hermitian metric on $\mathbb C^4$ and give $\mathcal O_Z(-2)$ its induced Hermitian metric. On the incidence chart $\lambda_1\ne0$, set $t=\lambda_2/\lambda_1$, $\mu_1/\lambda_1=z_1-\bar z_2t$, and $\mu_2/\lambda_1=z_2+\bar z_1t$. The horizontal complex directions of type $(0,1)$ are spanned by

$$H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2},\qquad H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1};$$

They annihilate the displayed holomorphic coordinates. Together with the vertical vector $\partial_{\bar t}$ they form a direct frame of $T^{0,1}Z$ on this chart, splitting it into horizontal and vertical subbundles. Their projections to $T_{\mathbb C}S^4$ form the complex alpha-plane at $[1:t]$; on $\lambda_1=0$ the same plane and splitting are defined by the second projective chart. The line bundle $\mathcal O_Z(-1)$ is the tautological holomorphic line bundle and $\mathcal O_Z(-2)=\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\otimes2}$.

items.title: Incidence alpha planes detect positive-orientation anti-self-duality
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement: At a finite point of the positively oriented stereographic chart in the definition of the incidence geometry, let $A$ be a smooth connection and $F_A$ its curvature. For $t\in\mathbb C$, evaluate $F_A$ on $H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2}$ and $H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1}$. Then $F_A(H_1,H_2)=0$ for every $t\in\mathbb C$ if and only if the self-dual part $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$ vanishes at that point. The same equivalence holds at the omitted projective value $t=\infty$ by using the second incidence chart.

items.title: Dolbeault groups of the negative twistor-fibre twists
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Let $L=\mathbb CP^1$ and let $\mathcal O_L(k)$ be the degree-$k$ holomorphic line bundle. For the smooth Dolbeault complexes on $L$, the cohomology groups satisfy

$$H^{0,0}_{\bar\partial}(L,\mathcal O_L(-1))=H^{0,1}_{\bar\partial}(L,\mathcal O_L(-1))=H^{0,0}_{\bar\partial}(L,\mathcal O_L(-2))=0,\qquad H^{0,1}_{\bar\partial}(L,\mathcal O_L(-2))\cong\mathbb C.$$

The canonical bundle is $K_L\cong\mathcal O_L(-2)$; the last group is one-dimensional, and the first three vanish.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited from harmonic-star duality.

items.title: Injective fibre-harmonic edge for coupled Penrose cohomology
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Assume full AC and the following analytic comparison: for $r\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, every finite-rank holomorphic vector bundle $G$ on $X=\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ has a canonical isomorphism $H^q(X,\mathcal O(G))\cong H^q_{\bar\partial}(X,G)$ for every $q\ge0$, and for $G=\mathcal O_X$ one has $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=\mathbb C$ and $H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)=0$ for $q>0$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth finite-rank Hermitian bundle with smooth unitary connection $A$, and let $F$ be a holomorphic bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ smoothly identified with $\pi^*E$ so that its Dolbeault operator is the ordinary vertical Dolbeault operator and the connection-horizontal alpha-plane operator from the incidence definition. Fibrewise harmonic projection of a global Dolbeault representative defines a linear map

$$\mathcal P_A:H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))\longrightarrow\Gamma(S^4,E).$$

Every global closed representative $\alpha$ has a unique decomposition $\alpha=\alpha_H+s\sigma+\bar\partial_F\gamma$, where $s=\mathcal P_A[\alpha]$, $\alpha_H$ is horizontal, $\sigma$ is the normalized fibre-harmonic generator, and the vertical correction $\gamma$ is smooth and glues over the base. The map is well defined and injective. The analytic comparison input is a conditional premise of this statement until its planned batch-67 carrier and proof are present and current.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC through the conditional analytic Dolbeault comparison and harmonic theory.

items.title: Round coupled Penrose correction gives the R-over-six operator
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Assume the conditional analytic comparison and the hypotheses of the injective-edge lemma, with $A$ a smooth unitary anti-self-dual connection. For a cohomology class $\xi\in H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))$, let $s=\mathcal P_A(\xi)$ be its fibre-harmonic image. The unique correction of $s\sigma$ that removes the horizontal-vertical component of its Dolbeault differential has remaining component $(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+2)s$ in a nonvanishing local frame. Consequently

$$\mathcal P_A\bigl(H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))\bigr)\subseteq\ker(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+2).$$

The scalar term is $R/6$ for the specified unit round metric, where $R=12$.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited from the conditional analytic edge input.

items.title: Coupled Penrose vanishing on the round four-sphere
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $S^4$ have the unit round metric and the positive stereographic orientation for $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$. Let $E\to S^4$ be any smooth finite-rank Hermitian bundle with a smooth unitary anti-self-dual connection $A$. On $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ use the incidence equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$, with infinity fibre $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. Suppose $F$ is a holomorphic bundle smoothly identified with $\pi^*E$ and its Dolbeault operator is the ordinary vertical derivative and the $A$-horizontal alpha-plane operator. Then

$$H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=H^1(Z,F^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=0.$$

This applies to arbitrary reducible and flat summands. It assumes no algebraic-to-analytic GAGA, monad, or inverse ADHM normal form as an independent premise.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited through the analytic sheaf/Dolbeault comparison and harmonic inputs.

items.title: Flat summands in coupled Penrose vanishing
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement: For any integer $m\ge0$, let $E=S^4\times\mathbb C^m$ have its standard Hermitian metric and trivial unitary connection, and let $F=\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus m}$ be the induced holomorphic bundle on the twistor space. Then $H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=H^1(Z,F^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))=0$. The fibre-harmonic transform and its dual act componentwise, so adjoining this flat summand preserves the coupled vanishing conclusion.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited from the conditional theorem inputs.

items.title: Local transforms versus global injectivity
items.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
items.statement: Let $U_N$ and $U_S$ be the two stereographic charts of $S^4$, and let $\xi\in H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))$ be a global class under the coupled theorem's hypotheses. On each chart compute the fibre-harmonic section from a global closed Dolbeault representative. On $U_N\cap U_S$ the two local sections agree because they are the harmonic projection on the same fibre and are unchanged by replacing the representative by a Dolbeault-exact form. If the glued section is zero, the global class is zero by injectivity. Thus a local contour expression alone establishes neither compatibility on the overlap nor injectivity of the global class map.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited from the conditional analytic comparison and fibrewise Hodge theory.
